title: Variant interoperability census: tokenizer/KV/context/tooling parity maintenance
creator: Maya Singh
description: Maintain and expand the Variant Interoperability Census (the canonical ledger we use for smart routing fallbacks) to ensure tokenizer, context-length, KV/cache semantics, and tooling hooks are compatible across primary and fallback model variants. This ticket bounds the maintenance work for the next quarter: audit current entries, add missing interoperability assertions, automate parity checks in CI, and wire census visibility into the Console routing diagnoser.
acceptance_criteria: Canonical census document updated with coverage for all active routing fallback pairs (hosted + dedicated + private)
Automated parity tests added to runtime CI that validate tokenizer tokenization equivalence for 5 representative prompt cohorts per model family
KV/cache behavior assertions (prefix caching, cache key determinism) added for each variant and validated in replay harness
Console routing diagnoser surfaces mismatch warnings for any future changes to tokenizer/context/kv signature
No regressions observed in canary traffic (latency or generation divergence > threshold) after rolling updated census-based routing checks
implementation_plan: 1) Inventory: generate list of all variants currently referenced in smart routing policies via routing-config-table export
2) Gap analysis: run tokenizer parity script (tools/tokenizer_census.py) across canonical prompt set and record disagreement rates per variant-pair
3) KV semantics: run KV replay for 3 prefix lengths and assert cache hit determinism; capture failures to compat ledger
4) Automate: add CI job 'variant-parity' that runs on model onboarding PRs and daily cron; failures create issue with prefilled repro data
5) Console: add UI hook to show census status + last-audit date in routing diagnoser (frontend ticket to follow)
6) Rollout: canary checks enabled for 2% of routing traffic in us-west-2 for 72h, monitor divergence and latency SLOs
7) Remediation: for non-trivial divergences propose mitigation (tokenizer shim, model aliasing, or exclude-from-fallback) and track remediation PRs
progress_updates: 2025-02-18: Kickoff — scoped inventory and created canonical export. Assigned Noah to own automation scripts.
2025-02-24: Inventory complete — found 42 variant entries used in routing policies across hosted and dedicated. Export attached.
2025-02-27: Initial tokenizer parity run completed for prompt cohort A (news/customer-support). 6 variant-pairs show >1% tokenization mismatch; adding to gap analysis.
2025-03-03: KV replay harness integrated into local testing; two variants show nondeterministic cache keys when prefix length > 1024. Filed follow-up remediation tasks.
2025-03-05: CI job prototype merged to feature branch; flaky thresholds tuned. Planning canary rollout for 2025-03-18 pending frontend diagnoser stub.
notes: Trade-offs considered: tokenizer shims add latency and complexity; prefer model aliasing when determinism can't be guaranteed.
We limit parity CI to the canonical cohort set to keep runtime short (~10m); full cohort audit is a separate ticket if failures are frequent.
Edge case: private on-prem variants may use bespoke tokenizers; rely on customer-provided attestations and add manual checklist entries for Private deployments.
